subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — SKU tiers, ramp acceleration, and flexible start
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@hydrolytics.ai>
To: logan_wright@redwoodai.com
Cc: procurement@hydrolytics.ai
Date: 2026-12-03T08:12:00-05:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — baseline usage + request for committed pricing

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Attached is a short usage matrix (recent 90-day token/embedding volumes and peak concurrent streams) so your team can size a dedicated pool for our primary inference workloads.

We have three commercial questions up front:
- Committed term: we prefer a 24-month reserved commit but can consider 12 or 36 if the economics move. What discount band do you offer for 12/24/36?
- Start flexibility: procurement has a target start date in mid-Feb (they may need a phased start across regions). Can you support a delayed activation and phased ramp?
- Throughput SLA: we need guidance on per-GPU throughput guarantees (tokens/s or streams) — and whether burst capacity is included.

Can you review the attached and send a SKU-level proposal (GPU type, pool size, target throughput, and the associated committed pricing)? Procurement would like to see a clear mapping between our usage tiers and the commit bands.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of AI Infrastructure
Hydrolytics

Attachment: hydrolytics-usage-matrix.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

From: logan_wright@redwoodai.com
To: Samira Khan <samira@hydrolytics.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodai.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com
Date: 2026-12-03T10:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — SKU tiers, ramp acceleration, and flexible start

Hi Samira — thanks for the matrix, that’s exactly what we needed. I took a first pass with Ben and Neha on sizing and options and outlined three paths below. I’m attaching a compact SKU proposal (PDF) that maps your projected 6/12/24-month volumes to reserved commits.

High-level options (short):
1) 12-month starter: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs, 75% utilization target, 10% discount to on-demand with 8-week start window. Good if you need faster termination flexibility.
2) 24-month balanced: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs + 4x burst-capacity GPUs (shared pool), 20% discount, throughput SLOs per GPU (baseline 220k tokens/s for our medium seq model), phased regional activation (US first, EU on month 3). 60-day guaranteed start window.
3) 36-month anchor: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs, dedicated burst pool, 26% discount, priority capacity routing and 99.9% uptime SLA for the pool. Includes two scheduled ramp checkpoints (month 3 & month 9) with crediting for missed throughput targets.

Key clarifications we’ll need from procurement so we can lock pricing:
- Firm preferred start month (actual activation triggers billing)
- Whether you want the burst pool to be reserved or on-demand (affects discount math)
- Any hard latency P95 targets per route (we can model throughput vs latency tradeoffs)

I’ll let Ben add the margin/discount mechanics and Neha note any security/enterprise terms that impact pricing. Happy to set a 30-minute sync with procurement next week to go through the SKU table.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Head of Sales — Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sku-proposal-v3.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)

From: ben_carter@redwoodai.com
To: Samira Khan <samira@hydrolytics.ai>, logan_wright@redwoodai.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com
Date: 2026-12-04T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — pricing mechanics and commit bands

Samira / Logan — quick breakdown of how the discounts move and how ramp credits work so procurement has something concrete to evaluate.

Discount geometry (example):
- 12m: base commit discount = 10% off hosted unit price; early upsell accelerator = additional 3% if you expand committed GPU count >25% within first 6 months.
- 24m: base = 20%; expansion accelerator = 5% for year-2 if committed usage grows per our growth band.
- 36m: base = 26%; includes 3% loyalty credit applied to final invoice for full-term completion.

Ramp and start flexibility: we can support a phased activation where only a portion of the pool is billable until you flip the regional activation flags (we call these "activation milestones"). Billing model options:
A) Billing on activation: customer only pays for GPU units marked as active. Reduces out-of-pocket risk if procurement needs a delayed start.
B) Billing on reservation (preferred economics): customer pays full reserved commit from agreed start date; we credit for under-utilized months via ramp credits to avoid waste. Credit formula example: if utilization < 60% in months 1-3, we apply a one-time credit equal to X% of monthly commit (calculated off projected baseline).

Throughput guarantees & SLAs:
- We guarantee baseline throughput per GPU for supported model families. For your medium seq-1 models, baseline = 220k tokens/s per GPU with 95th percentile latencies at typical batch sizes; burst capacity offers a 2x temporary throughput for up to 10 minutes per hour.
- If we fail to meet guaranteed throughput at the pool-level for more than 2 consecutive measurement windows, we apply service credits or provide additional burst hours as remediation.

Procurement items to surface: preferred billing model (A vs B), exact preferred start month, and whether you want the accelerator clauses (they reduce price but require commit expansion targets).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
On a related note: Neha, please flag any enterprise terms that could materially change the margin (eg. extended RPO, custom compliance testing).

From: Samira Khan <samira@hydrolytics.ai>
To: logan_wright@redwoodai.com, ben_carter@redwoodai.com
Cc: Hydrolytics Procurement <procurement@hydrolytics.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T11:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — pricing mechanics and commit bands

Thanks Logan/Ben — very helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement and infra:
- Procurement prefers the 24-month balanced option but requires a billing model that avoids paying for inactive regional capacity if the EU activation slips; they asked whether model A (billing on activation) can be applied to the EU region only while US billing follows model B.
- On the discount accelerator: we like the expansion incentive but need clearer KPIs — is expansion measured as committed GPU count or average util tokens/month? Procurement also wants a hard cap on the maximum cumulative discount and a clear clawback if we fail to hit the expansion bands.
- Start-month: target activation for US in 2027-02 (mid-Feb) with EU activation targeted for 2027-05. Procurement indicated a procurement board review in early Jan that could shift EU activation by +60 days.

Also, our infra lead asked whether Redwood will allow a one-quarter trial buffer (4 weeks) where we can run a pilot on 2 GPUs inside the reserved pool with no additional fee (to validate integration). That would make procurement more comfortable signing a 24-month commit.

Can you confirm whether a hybrid billing model (US = B, EU = A) is feasible, provide the exact expansion KPI definition, and confirm the pilot buffer possibility?

Best,
Samira

> Attachment: hydrolytics-usage-matrix.csv (as previously shared)

From: logan_wright@redwoodai.com
To: Samira Khan <samira@hydrolytics.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodai.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com
Date: 2026-12-07T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — SKU tiers, ramp acceleration, and flexible start

Samira — quick answers and next steps so procurement has something to take into the board: 

1) Hybrid billing: yes, we can do US = Billing on reservation (B) and EU = Billing on activation (A). We'll document the regions and activation flags in the SOW so there's no ambiguity on invoicing.

2) Expansion KPI definition: expansion is measured as incremental committed GPU-months (not raw tokens). Example: baseline = 12 committed GPUs; an accelerator triggers if committed GPUs increase by >= 25% sustained for at least two consecutive months. Clawback language: if expansion target is not maintained for year-2, we offset previously applied accelerator against final year invoices. We'll put a maximum cumulative discount cap (example: 30% max across all incentives).

3) Pilot buffer: we can offer a four-week pilot on 2 GPUs inside the reserved pool at no additional charge, provided the pilot runs prior to the formal activation date and we have a short integration checklist signed by both parties. Pilot hours will be logged and excluded from expansion calculations.

Next steps: I’ll update the SKU PDF to reflect hybrid billing and the accelerator KPIs and send a redlineable SOW for procurement review by Thursday. If that works, can we set a 30-minute procurement sync for Jan 5 (your local time) to walk the board materials?

If procurement confirms mid-Feb US activation and a May EU activation (with the 60-day slip window), we can model the invoice schedule and present a final commercial term sheet.

Thanks — talk soon,
Logan Wright
Head of Sales — Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
